title: Cross-border maritime actors can rehearse an infrastructure response before real-incident performance is known
source_unit: European External Action Service official account of MARSEC EU 26, a Finnish-hosted maritime security exercise involving EU member-state authorities, EU agencies, coast guards, commercial actors, and emergency services
geography: Baltic Sea and North Sea operational scenario; Finland-hosted exercise with Finnish, Polish, French, EU-agency, and commercial participation

denominator.unit: exercise components: tabletop exercise, LIVEX 1, and LIVEX 2

scenario.value: suspicious vessel conducting abnormal activity near undersea cables and possible infrastructure damage

information_phase.value: command centers exchanged vessel information and developed a shared maritime picture

operational_phase.value: boarding, search, securing, first aid, evacuation, firefighting, hazardous-space operations, and vessel control were practiced

observations.method: EEAS official exercise account describing the tabletop and two live operational phases; rehearsal activity is kept separate from a real incident outcome.
observations.uncertainty: The exercise does not measure response time or success during an actual cable or pipeline incident, nor does it establish attribution, deterrence, repair, or infrastructure continuity.
observations.subgroup: Finnish Border Guard-led exercise participants and cooperating maritime, law-enforcement, defense, emergency, and commercial actors.
observations.counterinterpretation: A realistic exercise can identify gaps and improve coordination without proving that the same chain would work under political pressure, weather, legal conflict, or a real attack.

denominator.unit: officially described MARSEC EU 26 cooperation network

national_authorities.value: Finnish Border Guard, Finnish authorities, Polish Border Guard, Finnish Defence Forces, Police, emergency healthcare, and rescue authorities

french_participation.value: French Navy participated in a preparatory phase

observations.method: Official participant and role description in the EEAS exercise account.
observations.uncertainty: Participation demonstrates a coordination interface, not equal authority, shared rules, public consent, cost sharing, or a guarantee that commercial actors would cooperate in a real incident.
observations.subgroup: Public authorities, EU agencies, military, emergency responders, coast guards, and commercial maritime operators.
observations.counterinterpretation: A multi-actor exercise may improve interoperability while also exposing unresolved jurisdiction, ownership, liability, or information-sharing conflicts.

denominator.unit: real incident, infrastructure owner, affected community, or later external actor response not included in the exercise account

institutional_learning.value: exercise lessons may inform future exercises and real-world operations

integrated_surveillance.value: the exercise tested the Integrated Surveillance Mechanism as a regional information-sharing hub

unmeasured_endpoint.value: actual repair, service continuity, attribution, deterrence, local burden, and public legitimacy

observations.method: Bounded interpretation of the official exercise purpose and described mechanisms; no causal or real-incident claim is made.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not follow a cable, pipeline, vessel, owner, community, or government through an actual incident and later outcome.
observations.subgroup: Critical-underwater-infrastructure stakeholders and cross-border maritime authorities; affected publics are not observed.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exercises can be politically meaningful signals of solidarity even without a measured deterrence effect or operational test under real conditions.

related_sources.claim: NATO describes Baltic Sentry as a separate enhanced-vigilance response to incidents involving critical undersea infrastructure.

boundary: This record establishes a cross-border exercise and an observable response chain around suspected undersea-infrastructure damage. It does not establish real-incident success, attribution, repair, continuity, deterrence, jurisdictional agreement, public acceptance, cost sharing, or changed external behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official EEAS exercise page used for the extracted findings; NATO context is linked but not used as the primary extraction source.
